classification: Existing browser-approval/session management repair. Actual mounted HTTP and deterministic owner controls; not browser UI, native browser, OS restart, SSD, updater or full epic acceptance.
failure: Session-only approvals had live cookies but no visible management descriptor, and revocation could remove authority while reporting refusal. Pending request retirement at five minutes could also discard the only management metadata.
repair: Reuse bounded in-memory request metadata for session-only management; never persist once-only authority. Completed live records remain only for their actual session/grant lifetime. Dead, revoked or evicted sessions release metadata and request capacity immediately.

Registry inspection exposes an owner-only non-touching snapshot using existing expiry semantics. Management polling does not refresh another session or extend inactivity, absolute lifetime or approval grants.
Completion challenge issuance and proof both enforce the original request deadline, including equality. Retaining management metadata does not extend eligibility to mint or rotate.

Descriptors distinguish remembered from session-only decisions. Rotation retains management identity. Revocation acknowledges any removed stored grant, live associated session or pending approved decision and retires only matching challenges.
The existing Activity Log state operation adds bounded counts for pending requests, session-only approvals and remembered approvals. No body, bearer, key, signature or identifier is logged.
